children: will be reporting results this Thursday morning. Here’s what you need to know.

MasterCraft beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $78.21 million, up 3% year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and full-year revenue guidance beating analysts’ expectations.
Is MasterCraft a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting MasterCraft’s revenue to grow 30.2% year on year, improving from the 18.4% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. MasterCraft has a history of exceeding Wall Street’s expectations.

Looking at MasterCraft’s peers in the consumer discretionary - leisure products segment, some have already reported their Q2 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Smith & Wesson delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 32.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 14.1%, and Ruger reported revenues up 19.3%, topping estimates by 23%. Smith & Wesson traded up 5.1% following the results while Ruger was also up 3.3%.

In the last year or so, investors have shifted their focus from one macro dynamic to the next (AI disintermediation and AI investment to geopolitical conflict, interest rates, and the health of the wider economy). While some of the consumer discretionary - leisure products stocks have shown solid performance in this choppy environment, the group has generally underperformed, with share prices down 6.3% on average over the last month. MasterCraft is down 1.8% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $27.60 (compared to the current share price of $23.64).
